blocks.text: Quick verdict

NodeMaven is the better choice for social media, multi-accounting and anti-detect browser users: pre-screened IPs, long sticky sessions, rollover, cashback and a $2.20/GB monthly rate that beats Infatica's $3.60/GB at 100 GB. Infatica is the better choice for location-precise data collection that needs ZIP targeting, for IPv6 residential IPs, and for procurement teams that require sourcing documentation and ISO certifications, and its $40 for 10 GB is cheaper than NodeMaven's $45 pay-as-you-go.

NodeMaven and Infatica are both mid-sized residential networks with roughly 30-40 million advertised IPs, and both sell mobile and ISP proxies. NodeMaven's selling point is its IP Quality Filter, which screens IPs before assignment for account-sensitive work. Infatica's selling points are ZIP targeting on every plan, an IPv6 residential pool, a written no-reselling policy and ISO certifications. This comparison helps you choose by workload.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven is the quality-first option. Instead of handing out whatever IP the pool returns, it screens addresses in real time and lets you choose how strict the screening is. That matters most for account-based work such as social media management and multi-accounting, where a flagged IP can cost you an account. The price reflects it: $4.50/GB without a plan and $2.20/GB on monthly plans.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
Infatica in 2026: what you get

Infatica pitches itself on ethical sourcing and features available to every customer. All residential plans include country, city and ZIP targeting, IP whitelisting and selectable rotation times, and a 7-day $4 trial lowers the risk of testing. Independent reviewers have found its proxies fast and its pool modest but respectable. Its niche extra is a premium IPv6 residential pool, rare in this market, at about 1.5x the normal per-GB price.

Strengths: ZIP targeting included on every plan; Clear sourcing policy and ISO certifications; Cheap 7-day trial; Rare IPv6 residential pool. Weak spots: Mid-range pool size; Per-GB price stays above $3.50 until large volumes; Subscription traffic does not roll over.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs Infatica

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

Infatica charges $4/GB pay-as-you-go for residential traffic. Subscriptions cost $3.84/GB at 25 GB, $3.60/GB at 100 GB, and fall to about $2.70/GB at 500 GB and $2.60/GB at 1 TB. Premium IPv6 residential runs at roughly 1.5x those rates, starting at $6/GB.

For a 10 GB month, Infatica costs about $40 while NodeMaven costs about $45, so Infatica saves around 11%. For a 100 GB month, NodeMaven costs about $220 while Infatica costs about $360, so NodeMaven saves around 39%. The sticker price is only half of it. NodeMaven's unused traffic carries forward, while Infatica's does not (subscription traffic resets monthly), so if your usage swings from month to month NodeMaven can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

On paper the two networks are similar in size: NodeMaven advertises 30M+ residential + 250K mobile residential IPs and Infatica advertises 35M-40M. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and Infatica lists 195. On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while Infatica offers country, state, city and ZIP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and Infatica offers per-request rotation or selectable rotation times. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Infatica wins. The deciding factor for Infatica: fast proxies that did well on popular targets in independent tests. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: the quality filter matters less for high-rotation crawling.

SERP and rank tracking: Infatica wins. The deciding factor for Infatica: ZIP targeting helps local search results. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need.

Social media and multi-account management: NodeMaven wins. The deciding factor for NodeMaven: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. The limitation on the Infatica side: rotation controls are good but very long sticky sessions are not a headline feature.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Infatica wins. The deciding factor for Infatica: ZIP-level targeting for local prices. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: fine for light checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Infatica wins. The deciding factor for Infatica: precise geo targeting and clean sourcing. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: good quality but a smaller pool.

Tight budgets: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG. With Infatica: mid-range pricing until you reach large volumes. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. Infatica: 7-day trial for $4 (residential) or $8 (mobile). Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. Infatica: Standard verification; states it does not resell IPs. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and Infatica before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle NodeMaven vs Infatica faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; Infatica: 7-day trial for $4 (residential) or $8 (mobile)).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 1, Infatica in 4, and 1 is a tie. That makes Infatica the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while Infatica is strongest for compliance-conscious buyers. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
